title: Choucroute Garnie
description: Choucroute garnie is an Alsatian staple in which at least four types of pork are braised with sauerkraut and white wine and loads of aromatics for a fragrant one-pot meal. After braising, the pork is sliced and served with an array of mustards and crusty bread for an interactive dish perfect for a crowd.
ingredients: ¼ cup duck fat (or oil/butter combo)
1 pound double-smoked slab bacon, halved lengthwise (or thick cut bacon or salt pork)
½ rack (1 pound) baby back ribs, halved crosswise (or boneless country ribs)
1 apple, peeled, cored, and roughly chopped
1½ cups dry white wine (preferably an Alsatian Riesling)
1 pound baby red-skin potatoes (or quartered other potatoes)
directions: In an 8-quart Dutch oven, heat the duck fat over medium-high heat. Working in batches, cook the kielbasa, bacon, bratwurst and ribs, turning as needed, until golden brown, 4 to 6 minutes for the kielbasa and bacon, and 6 to 8 minutes for the bratwurst and ribs. Transfer each to a plate, leaving any dripping in the pot.
Add onions and saute until soft. Add garlic and apple, and cook, stirring, several minutes.

To the pot, add the sauerkraut, juniper berries, peppercorns, cloves, and bay leaves. Cook until warmed through and fragrant, 3 minutes. Add the reserved meats, the stock and white wine, and bring to a simmer.
On the stove top or in the over at 325 degrees, cook, covered, until the meat is tender, 1 hour. Add the potatoes and continue to cook until tender, 25 to 30 minutes more.
Transfer the meats to a cutting board and slice. Arrange on a platter with the braised sauerkraut and potatoes on the side, all with a sprinkling of parsley for color.
Serve with assorted mustards and crusty bread.
